data.narrative:
Xanadu Quantum Technologies is a public-stage quantum computing company that has raised $245M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five same-sector, same-stage companies: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Rigetti Computing ($4.5B), Infleqtion ($1.9B), and Archer Materials ($60M). This universe spans the full range of quantum computing valuations currently trading publicly, with a spread from $60M to $13.0B.

Peer-median triangulation, the primary applicable method given data constraints, yields an implied valuation of $4.5B. This reflects the midpoint of the five-company comp set and accounts for the significant heterogeneity in stage maturity and commercialization progress within the quantum computing sector. The peer range illustrates material dispersion: early-stage quantum plays trade substantially below the median, while market leaders command multiples significantly higher.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.8B to $5.2B centered on a median of $4.5B. Key uncertainties include the pace of technical milestones relative to peer companies, revenue generation and path to profitability, and near-term capital requirements relative to available cash. The wide dispersion in comparable valuations ($60M to $13.0B) reflects the nascent and heterogeneous nature of the quantum computing market, limiting the precision of any single point estimate.
